lines.trans: Good night, team! I refilled Salma's two big white jars so everything looks tidy for dawn!
Wait, Mazen—those two white ceramic jars had little paper labels underneath!
Oh, the paper got damp when I wiped the counter, so I threw both labels away.
Tell me both jars held sugar, boss. Please tell me both were sugar.
No, one bag was fine white caster sugar and one bag was fine white sea salt!
Which jar got the sugar, Mazen—the left jar or the right jar?!
Left! Definitely left! ... Or did I turn both jars around when I polished the lids?
If Nour whisks four spoons of sea salt into Wednesday's lemon tarts, the city clerk will run!
Don't panic—tomorrow at six we taste a tiny pinch on a clean spoon before baking!
Write a big red note right now, Nour! Wait—who is knocking at the front gate at ten at night?!
Look through the lobby window—a woman in a blue coat holding a city folder?!
Wait—isn't the city clerk supposed to come Wednesday at three, NOT Tuesday night?!

Goodbye!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for both casual 'yes / yeah' and 'oh! / ah!' upon noticing something.

examples.trans: Oh, the door opened! Thank you.
Yes, eight rooms and eight keys.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine حمرا (hamra); شاي أحمر means black tea.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or black tea?
There is a red ribbon on my suitcase.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

أصبح.gloss: to wake in the morning; become

meanings.en: to wake in the morning; become
meanings.note: Used nightly in the warm Levantine farewell تصبحوا على خير ('may you wake in goodness' = good night).

examples.text: تصبحوا على خير يا جماعة، منشوفكم الصبح!
examples.trans: Good night, everyone—we'll see you in the morning!

examples.text: تصبح على خير يا عمي، ارتاح الليلة.
examples.trans: Good night, uncle, get some rest tonight.

meanings.note: Used to express certainty or agreement.

examples.trans: Hello! You must be Nour.

examples.text: أكيد صاحبه رح يدور عليه قريبا.
examples.trans: Surely its owner will look for it soon.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Used as a question word or indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian everyday verb for 'to come' (إجا / بيجي).

examples.trans: You came ten minutes early.
I will come on Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Form VIII verb meaning 'get a fright / panic'.

examples.text: لا ترتعبوا، هي بس لوية خفيفة مش كسر.
examples.trans: Don't panic—it's just a mild twist, not a break.

examples.text: ارتعبت لما سمعت صوت الصحن بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: I panicked when I heard the sound of the plate in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The reception desk is beside the door.
Thank you for the warm welcome.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The guest arrived Wednesday night.
We meet on Wednesday morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: He called us on Tuesday.
The corner shop is open every Tuesday.

meanings.note: Used in ملح بحر ('sea salt') as well as for the Mediterranean or Dead Sea.

examples.text: حطيت رشة صغيرة من ملح البحر فوق العجينة.
examples.trans: I put a tiny pinch of sea salt on top of the dough.

examples.text: هوا البحر بيجي لطيف ومنعش آخر النهار.
examples.trans: The sea breeze comes in gentle and refreshing late in the afternoon.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'tomorrow' (بكرا الصبح 'tomorrow morning').

examples.text: بكرا الصبح رح نسبق المي الباردة!
examples.trans: Tomorrow morning we will beat the cold water!
We booked a quiet dinner — will you join us tomorrow?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بلديات.

examples.trans: He works in the contracts office at the municipality.
The municipal building is next to the square.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببين, بيبين).

examples.text: لما بدهم يبينوا هاديين بيتأخروا دقيقتين.
examples.trans: When they want to play it cool, they arrive two minutes late.
The truth came out at the end of the week.

meanings.note: Baked fruit or custard tart, especially تارت الليمون ('lemon tart').

examples.text: تارت الليمون بقشرة اللوز طلع أطيب واحد.
examples.trans: The lemon tart with the almond crust turned out to be the tastiest one.

examples.text: خلينا قطعة تارت صغيرة لطارق بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We saved a small slice of tart for Tariq in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Form V intransitive verb meaning 'get wet / soaked in the rain'.

examples.text: دخلنا الشيش جوا قبل ما يتبلل الخشب.
examples.trans: We brought the shutters inside before the wood got soaked.
My sleeves got a little wet from the rain.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Used to address a group of people informally, like 'guys' or 'folks' ('ya jamaa'a').

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
Come in, folks, the tea is ready.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحمل, بيحمل).

examples.text: بتحمل مفك بكل مكان يا طارق!
examples.trans: You carry a screwdriver everywhere, Tariq!
He picked up the wrong blue bag at the station.

meanings.note: Culinary verb for whisking eggs, lemon curd, or cream until smooth.

examples.text: نور بتخفق البيض مع الليمون والسكر بهدوء.
examples.trans: Nour whisks the eggs gently with lemon and sugar.

examples.text: خفقت سلمى الكريمة حتى صارت ناعمة ومتساوية.
examples.trans: Salma whisked the curd until it turned smooth and glossy.

meanings.note: Core word in صباح الخير ('good morning'), مساء الخير ('good evening'), تصبح على خير ('good night'), and rising-tone خير؟ ('is everything okay?').

examples.trans: Good morning, neighbours!

examples.text: خير إن شاء الله، شو صار؟
examples.trans: Hopefully all is well, what happened?

meanings.note: Verbal noun (masdar) disambiguated with fatha-sukun from noun خُبز ('bread').

examples.text: ريحة الخبز الطازة رح تعبي الساحة من الصبح.
examples.trans: The smell of fresh baking will fill the courtyard from early morning.

examples.text: وقت الخبز بالفرن عشرين دقيقة بالتمام.
examples.trans: The baking time in the oven is twenty minutes sharp.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine hollow verb (from Classical ذاق, with ذ -> د); imperative دوق / دوقي ('taste!').

examples.text: دوقي هالمربى الحلو قبل ما نشتري المرطبان.
examples.trans: Taste this sweet jam before we buy the jar.
Ziad tasted the honey and smiled right away.

meanings.note: Past tense verb for knocking on a door, hammering a nail, or sometimes calling someone on the phone ('daqq 'ala').

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast!
The clock tower started chiming twelve.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Used mainly in polite/earnest requests: أرجوك (to a man), أرجوكي (to a woman), أرجوكم (plural) — 'please!'.

examples.trans: Please write down that sentence!
Please do not open the white parcel.

meanings.note: Standard Levantine kitchen term for the work counter (originally a slab of marble, رخام).

examples.text: مسحنا الرخامة ورتبنا مرتبانات السكر والملح.
examples.trans: We wiped the countertop and arranged the sugar and salt jars.

examples.text: فرد طارق العجينة الرقيقة عالرخامة الباردة.
examples.trans: Tariq rolled the thin dough out on the cool counter.

meanings.note: Instance noun from رش ('sprinkle/spray'): رشة ملح = 'a pinch of salt'.

examples.text: الشوربة بدها بس رشة ملح وعصرة ليمون.
examples.trans: The soup just needs a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon.

examples.text: حطي رشة قرفة ناعمة فوق الفنجان.
examples.trans: Put a light sprinkle of ground cinnamon on top of the cup.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Respectful and warm Levantine title for a woman ('Madam / Mrs. / lady').

examples.text: يسلموا إيديكي يا ست سعاد عاللحن الحلو.
examples.trans: Bless your hands, Madam Suad, for the lovely melody.

examples.text: كل ست وشيخ بالحارة معزومين عالافتتاح.
examples.trans: Every lady and elder on the lane is invited to the opening.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I like black tea without sugar.
We sprinkled powdered sugar over the cake.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطل, بيطل).

examples.text: مازن بيطل من ورا الستارة كل دقيقة!
examples.trans: Mazen peeks from behind the curtain every minute!
The window overlooks the courtyard and the tree.

meanings.note: Form II Jordanian verb for filling buckets, cups, or rooms with light.

examples.trans: We filled the two buckets with warm soapy water.
Morning sunlight fills the room with brightness.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: The standalone number ten.

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Refers to a lid, cover, or sometimes a blanket.

examples.trans: Put the lid on the pot.
In winter I sleep under a heavy blanket.

meanings.note: Early pre-sunrise morning (الفجر), prime baking hour in Levantine bakeries.

examples.text: الخبازين بيصحوا قبل الفجر عشان يخبزوا العجين.
examples.trans: Bakers wake up before dawn to bake the dough.

examples.text: هوا الفجر بعمان بيكون بارد ومنعش كتير.
examples.trans: Dawn air in Amman is crisp and deeply refreshing.

meanings.note: Handcrafted fired clay vessels and cups, a staple of Jordanian and Levantine street markets.

examples.text: اشترينا إبريق وفناجين من بسطة الفخار.
examples.trans: We bought a pitcher and cups from the pottery stall.

examples.text: المي ببريق الفخار بتضل باردة بالصيف.
examples.trans: Water in a clay pitcher stays cool in summer.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Preposition and adverb for time or sequence meaning 'prior to' or 'before'.

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

كب.gloss: to spill; pour out; pour down (rain)

meanings.en: to spill; pour out; pour down (rain)
meanings.note: Quintessential Jordanian verb for spilling coffee, throwing out water, or rain pouring down (عم تكب مطر).

examples.text: امسك الفنجان منيح قبل ما تكب القهوة.
examples.trans: Hold the cup steady before you spill the coffee.

examples.text: السما بلشت تكب مطر بنص الليل.
examples.trans: The sky started pouring rain at midnight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Depending on vowels, it means 'he wrote' (katab) or plural 'books' (kutub).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كياس.

examples.trans: Give me a cloth bag for the shop.
I carried the bag of apples and bread.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلبس, بيلبس).

examples.text: أنا أكيد ما بلبس مقاس أربعة وأربعين!
examples.trans: I certainly do not wear size forty-four!

examples.text: لبس معطفه قبل ما يطلع بالمطر.
examples.trans: He put on his coat before going out in the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلف, بيلف).

examples.text: لفي شمال برا البوابة وامشي دغري.
examples.trans: Turn left outside the gate and walk straight.
Turn left at the stair landing.

meanings.note: Common conjunction used to introduce a time clause, distinct from the question word 'when' (mita).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلمع, بيلمع).

examples.trans: Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

examples.text: خمستعشر سنة وأنا بلمع مفاتيح النحاس!
examples.trans: Fifteen years I have been polishing the brass keys!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليالي.

examples.trans: The guest arrived last night.
The neighbourhood is very quiet at night.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Used to describe a neat person, a well-organized room, or generally something of high quality (e.g. 'a nice car').

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting right away.
Neat pencil sketches.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine pantry word (also pronounced مرطبان) for glass storage jars (dual مرتبانين).

examples.text: حطيت مرتبانين قزاز كبار عالرف: واحد سكر وواحد ملح.
examples.trans: I put two big glass jars on the shelf: one sugar and one salt.

examples.text: لزقنا ملصق واضح على كل مرتبان بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We stuck a clear label onto every jar in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسح, بيمسح).

examples.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate.
We wiped down the tables before breakfast.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: معاطف.

examples.trans: Take off your heavy coat and rest.
Hang the grey coat beside the door.

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Used with الـ (المفروض + imperfect verb) to mean 'is supposed to'.

examples.text: المفروض ينشف الدهان تماما قبل الساعة ستة.
examples.trans: The paint is supposed to dry completely before six o'clock.

examples.text: كان المفروض نركب الشيش العصر بس بلشت تمطر.
examples.trans: We were supposed to hang the shutters in the afternoon, then it started raining.

meanings.note: Essential kitchen noun; ملح بحر = 'sea salt'.

examples.text: إوعك تخربط بين مرتبان السكر ومرتبان الملح!
examples.trans: Don't ever mix up the sugar jar and the salt jar!

examples.text: حطيت نص معلقة ملح بالعجين قبل الخبز.
examples.trans: I added half a spoonful of salt to the dough before baking.

meanings.note: Dual ملصقين ('the two labels'), plural ملصقات ('labels / stickers').

examples.text: نور كتبت ملصقات واضحة وكبيرة لكل المرتبانات.
examples.trans: Nour wrote big, clear labels for all the jars.

examples.text: تأكد إن الملصقين ناشفين قبل ما تمسك القزاز.
examples.trans: Make sure both labels are dry before you pick up the glass.

meanings.note: In spoken Jordanian, standard ملعقة shifts consonants to معلقة (ma'laqa), plural معالق (ma'aaliq).

examples.text: حطي معلقة صغيرة جنب كل فنجان.
examples.trans: Put a small spoon beside every cup.
The silver spoons are in the top drawer.

meanings.note: Front-desk binder or document folder (from لف 'wrap/fold').

examples.text: نور رتبت قوائم المطبخ بملف الاستقبال الأخضر.
examples.trans: Nour organized the kitchen checklists in the green front-desk folder.

examples.text: كل الفواتير والمخططات محفوظة بنفس الملف.
examples.trans: All the receipts and floor plans are kept in the same folder.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: موظفة). Plural: موظفين.

examples.trans: I am the new receptionist at the guesthouse.
All the staff here are helpful and friendly.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun used for people.

examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?
Whose is this brown leather notebook?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناعمة, plural: ناعمين); سكر ناعم means 'powdered sugar'.

examples.trans: I brought two soft pillows for the attic.
Lemon cake dusted with powdered sugar.

meanings.note: Natural spoken Levantine pronunciation of نظيف ('clean'), broken plural نضاف.

examples.text: مسحنا الفرشاية بقماشة نضيفة ومي دافية.
examples.trans: We wiped the brush with a clean cloth and warm water.

examples.text: المطبخ صار نضيف ومرتب وجاهز لبكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: The kitchen is spotless, tidy, and ready for tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?
I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بهرب, بيهرب).

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
You left the bag on the doorstep and bolted!

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: One sheet of paper or one leaf; the collective ورق means paper in general.

examples.trans: Write your number down for me on a piece of paper.
The tree leaf turns yellow in autumn.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
